title: Sticky Context Allocator — scratch / rough PRD
body:
Purpose
---
Quick thought dump about a lightweight “sticky context allocator” that assigns small, reusable context windows to sessions/IDs to increase KV-cache reuse and reduce per-token compute for multi-turn systems. This is a personal scratchpad — not finalized.

Problem statement
- Many apps repeatedly send the same prefixes (instructions, system messages, short user profiles) across requests for a given sticky entity (user/session, conversation id, doc id).
- Current runtime caching is per-request/prefix-aware but misses cross-request affinity patterns when inputs vary slightly (minor system changes or injected metadata).
- Result: wasted decoding compute, higher latency and cost.

Proposal (high-level)
- Provide a thin allocation layer that:
  1) Creates a persistent context-slot for a given affinity key (session_id, user_id, doc_id, or combination).
  2) Stores a canonicalized prefix snapshot + tokenized KV-cache for that slot.
  3) At request time, the router can try to attach the slot (if matching policy) and reuse cached KV states or prefix tokens to avoid recomputation.
  4) Fall back to full generation when mismatch or policy denies reuse.

Core design goals
- Minimal API surface for early experiments.
- Opt-in per-customer and per-route.
- Respect privacy: slots are namespaced by customer & region; optional TTL or explicit erase.
- Be robust: cheap eviction, avoid correctness regressions (ensure prompt integrity).

User personas / Who benefits- Product teams with chat features (customer support, agents)- Knowledge-base assistants that maintain per-document context- Multi-turn assistant experiences with stable system messages

Success metrics (experiment)
- Cache hit rate for sticky slots (target 30% within week 1 for pilot workloads)
- Token compute reduction (%) and wall-time latency p95 change- Cost delta per 100K requests- No increase in wrong-answer rate (quality regressions) beyond tolerance

User stories (rough)
- As an SDK user, I can pin a route to enable sticky-context with a TTL and affinity key (e.g., session_id).
  Acceptance: API flag + quick metric that shows reduced initial tokenization for subsequent messages.
- As an operator, I can list and evict sticky slots for a tenant.
  Acceptance: admin API or Console table per-tenant with count/age/size and manual delete.
- As a privacy officer, I can configure default TTL and auto-wipe policies for sticky slots.
  Acceptance: policy enforced at allocation time and visible in Console.

Basic API sketch (very rough)
- client request fields: { route, input, affinity_key (optional), sticky_options (enable: bool, ttl_secs, canonicalize_rules) }
- router behavior: if enable and slot exists -> attempt attach and reuse KV cache; if attach fails, compute and optionally update slot.

Canonicalization heuristics (sketch)
- Normalize obvious temporal tokens (dates), redact volatile IDs, allow clients to specify patterns.
- Optionally store multiple canonical variants (small) per slot to handle minor differences.

Architecture considerations
- Storage: small LRU store per host (in-memory for fastest), backed by distributed slot index (metadata) in Redis/kvstore.
- Safety: each slot pinned to model variant/quantization profile; if serving model changes, invalidate slot.
- Eviction: size-based + TTL + LRU; ensure auto-trim to avoid OOM.
- Metrics: per-slot hit/miss, attach latency, slot-size distribution.

Experiment plan / rollout (MVP)
Phase 0 — sim/analysis
- Offline trace analysis: find affinity patterns in 2 weeks of hosted traffic (sampled). Create hypothesis list of top N prefixes. (JIRA: INF-3421)
Phase 1 — internal pilot
- Implement a local-only slot allocator behind a feature flag for a few internal routes (support-bot). Measure hit rates and regressions.
Phase 2 — external pilot (opt-in tenants)
- Expose API flag + console toggle; run with 3 customers; collect metrics and qualitative feedback.
Phase 3 — general availability
- Stabilize, add admin features, rollout guidelines, and SDK wrappers.

Monitoring and telemetry
- New metrics: sticky.slot.attaches, sticky.slot.hits, sticky.slot.evictions, avg_slot_bytes
- Tracing: tag requests with slot_id when attached; enable sampleable request snapshot to verify correctness.
- Alerting: sudden drop in API-level accuracy score or spike in slot-mismatch errors.

Open questions / risks
- Quality regressions when the canonicalized prefix differs subtly and influences generation context (how to detect subtle drift?)
- Memory overhead vs benefit: what is the break-even for average prefix length and reuse frequency?
- Multi-tenant isolation: how to guarantee no cross-tenant leakage in shared hosts?
- Concurrency: multiple simultaneous updates to one slot—need CAS/optimistic update semantics.
- Policy UX: how will non-technical users reason about canonicalization rules?

Quick runbook notes (notes-to-self)
- Start with tiny in-memory LRU per worker to keep iteration fast.
- Instrument a replay harness: play sampled requests through canary allocator to estimate hit rate without changing production responses.
- Add a safety toggle: "read-only attach" where we allow reuse but do not mutate slot state on miss; helps evaluate risk.
- Prototype token-diff comparator: log tokens saved per attach to compute token savings.

Action items / next steps
- [ ] Run trace query: count stable prefixes by session over last 14d (Id: INF-3421). -> ask SRE/data team for sample ETL.
- [ ] Spike: implement minimal slot attach API + in-process store. PR: draft on runtime repo. (see linked GH).
- [ ] Draft quick UX copy for Console toggle and admin table.
- [ ] Set up evaluation plan: metric dashboards and canary route.

Notes / stray ideas
- Could be used for embedding reuse too: store prefix embeddings to accelerate semantic search within context.
- Consider pairing with quality watchdog: if model output changes after attach, mark slot as "poisoned" and quarantine.
- Name iteration: "sticky context allocator" vs "session slot cache" vs "context pinning" — need marketing-friendly term.

References / related tickets
- JIRA INF-3421: affinity-trace-analysis
- GH PR 987: runtime small-cache-spike (prototype code to branch from)
- Confluence: INF-Sticky-Context (proto notes)

Personal notes: keep this lean and experiment-first. Prioritize a low-risk read-only attach mode for the first internal pilot so ops can review before mutation is enabled.

---
End of scratchpad (H. Brody)
